title: Water Damage
briefing: A landlord filed an insurance claim for a burst pipe that flooded a ground-floor unit. The adjuster wants a police report before they'll pay out — routine, except the tenant swears there was no pipe to burst.

location_hotspots.name: The flooded unit
location_hotspots.description: Water damage along one wall, oddly even for a 'burst pipe.'

location_hotspots.name: Basement pipes
location_hotspots.description: The building's plumbing, all of it, in one place.

location_hotspots.name: Landlord's office
location_hotspots.description: Filing cabinets going back a decade.

location_hotspots.name: Landlord's phone
location_hotspots.description: Sitting right there on the desk, unlocked.

evidence.name: Water stain pattern
evidence.description: The stain climbs evenly from floor to waist height along a single wall — consistent with a bucket, not a burst pipe.

evidence.name: Bone-dry pipe
evidence.description: The pipe the claim blames is dry, capped, and hasn't carried water in months.

evidence.name: Backdated repair invoice
evidence.description: An invoice for 'emergency plumbing repair,' dated the day of the flood, from a plumber who says he never went.

evidence.name: Texts to the plumber
evidence.description: The landlord, three days before the flood: 'just sign the invoice, you don't have to actually come out.'

evidence.name: Water mitigation invoice
evidence.description: A separate, unrelated-looking invoice from a 'water mitigation consultancy' buried in the same file. Paid in full, no follow-up. Not evidence of this fraud — just odd paperwork.

evidence.name: Neighbor's noise complaint
evidence.description: A neighbor complaining about renovation noise last month. Unrelated to the claim.

suspects.name: The landlord
suspects.motive: Insurance fraud — staged the flood to cover a renovation he didn't want to pay for out of pocket.
suspects.alibi: Says he was out of town when it happened. Was actually two floors up the whole time.

suspects.name: The plumber
suspects.motive: None — named on the invoice but denies doing the work.
suspects.alibi: Confirmed on another job site all day, three other clients vouch for him.

nodes.speaker_line: Terrible luck, that pipe. Old building.

options.text: Your plumber says he never came out.
Walk me through the timeline again.

nodes.speaker_line: He came by, I just... don't have a great memory for dates.

options.text: This invoice is backdated. You wrote it yourself.

nodes.speaker_line: ...Fine. The reno money fell through. Insurance doesn't ask questions about a burst pipe.

options.text: That's fraud, and you know it.

solution.correct_motive: Insurance fraud — staged flood damage to cover a renovation, using a friendly plumber's invoice as cover.
